anchors.contains: source revision -> build artifact -> test report -> deployment admission
Deployment approval is intentionally not implied by build or test success
Platform Operations owns the final production deployment admission decision
Until that conflict is reconciled, downstream consumers must preserve both owner claims
Test success is necessary evidence but is not production approval

system_architecture_tree.name: Build Worker
system_architecture_tree.responsibility: Build the exact admitted source revision into an immutable build artifact.
non_responsibilities: Does not establish test success or deployment approval.
system_architecture_tree.rationale: The committed pipeline declares the build stage and its owner.

system_architecture_tree.name: Deployment Admission
system_architecture_tree.responsibility: Evaluate whether a verified deployment candidate may proceed to production deployment.
non_responsibilities: Does not infer production approval from test success.
system_architecture_tree.rationale: Both pipeline and policy identify a distinct deployment-admission boundary.

system_architecture_tree.name: Source Control Boundary
system_architecture_tree.responsibility: Own exact source revision identity supplied to the delivery flow.
non_responsibilities: Does not prove that build, test, or deployment will succeed.
system_architecture_tree.rationale: The service description starts the delivery chain from a source revision.

system_architecture_tree.name: Mercury CI Service
system_architecture_tree.responsibility: Coordinate source, build, verification, and deployment-admission boundaries without collapsing their authorities.
system_architecture_tree.rationale: The source description and deployment policy define a bounded software-delivery service.

system_architecture_tree.name: Test Runner
system_architecture_tree.responsibility: Verify the exact build artifact and produce a bounded test result.
system_architecture_tree.rationale: The pipeline and policy distinguish test evidence from deployment authority.

module_responsibility_map.subject: Build execution and build artifact
module_responsibility_map.responsibility: Own build execution for the admitted source revision.
non_responsibilities: Does not own verification or deployment approval.
module_responsibility_map.rationale: The pipeline explicitly assigns the build stage to build automation.

module_responsibility_map.subject: Production deployment admission
module_responsibility_map.responsibility: Own the final production deployment admission decision.
non_responsibilities: Does not rewrite build or test evidence.
module_responsibility_map.rationale: Deployment policy assigns final admission to Platform Operations while the pipeline names release automation.

module_responsibility_map.subject: Production deployment admission
module_responsibility_map.responsibility: Prepare and submit deployment candidates and is currently named as the pipeline deploy-admission owner.
non_responsibilities: Must not be treated as sole accepted production deployment authority while the policy conflict remains.
module_responsibility_map.rationale: The committed pipeline and deployment policy disagree about final admission ownership.

module_responsibility_map.subject: Source revision identity
module_responsibility_map.responsibility: Own exact source revision identity entering the delivery chain.
module_responsibility_map.rationale: The service description defines source revision as the first bounded input.

module_responsibility_map.subject: Verification result
module_responsibility_map.responsibility: Own the bounded test result for the exact build artifact.
non_responsibilities: Does not own production deployment approval.
module_responsibility_map.rationale: The pipeline assigns test execution to verification automation.

implementation_intent_summary.subject: Build and test binding
implementation_intent_summary.statement: Verification must consume the exact build artifact produced from the admitted source revision.
implementation_intent_summary.rationale: The delivery chain separates revision, build artifact, and test report identities.

implementation_intent_summary.subject: Deployment governance
implementation_intent_summary.statement: Deployment admission remains a separate decision after verification.
implementation_intent_summary.rationale: Both README and deployment policy deny test-success-as-approval semantics.

validation_assurance_ownership.subject: Build artifact production
validation_assurance_ownership.responsibility: Produce the bounded build artifact for downstream verification.

validation_assurance_ownership.subject: Verification result
validation_assurance_ownership.responsibility: Produce test evidence without escalating it into production approval.
validation_assurance_ownership.rationale: Policy explicitly caps the test claim.

constraints.subject: Deployment admission
constraints.statement: Test success is not production approval.
constraints.rationale: Deployment policy requires an independent admission decision.

constraints.subject: Build input
constraints.statement: Build execution is bound to the exact admitted source revision.
constraints.rationale: The delivery chain begins from source revision identity.

unknowns.subject: Current production approval
unknowns.statement: No fixture evidence establishes that a production deployment has been approved.
unknowns.rationale: The fixture defines the decision boundary but contains no actual approval occurrence.

architecture_memory.claim_ceiling: This fixture establishes only bounded architecture, responsibility, evidence and authority semantics for a generic software-delivery service. It does not prove a real deployment, current production approval, exhaustive ownership, or operational readiness.

capabilities.name: Immutable artifact build
capabilities.mainline_rationale: Artifact build is a direct step in the service delivery chain.

capabilities.name: Deployment admission
capabilities.mainline_rationale: Deployment admission is a direct but independently governed delivery boundary.

capabilities.name: Build verification
capabilities.mainline_rationale: Verification is a direct evidence-producing step in the service delivery chain.

claim_ceiling: This non-WFF conformance fixture proves only that the supported general EKRI Architecture View, Capability Authority/L0-L3 queries and Flow/Handoff query can preserve exact evidence, identity, unknown and conflicting authority posture for an unrelated software-delivery system.
